citation: Mohammed Latif Siddiq et al. (2024). Using Large Language Models to Generate JUnit Tests: An Empirical Study. EASE '24: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering. doi:10.1145/3661167.3661216
dataset: HumanEval bản Java (160 lớp, lời giải Java do tác giả viết) và EvoSuite SF110 (194 lớp, 47 dự án)

main_result: HumanEval: dưới một nửa test của Codex (2K, 4K) và GPT-3.5-Turbo biên dịch được, StarCoder 70%; sửa heuristic tăng tỉ lệ biên dịch trung bình 41% (Codex 2K từ 37,5% lên 100%). citation: Jaskeerat Singh et al. (2026). A Qualitative and Quantitative Exploration of LLM-Based Test Generation Repair Loops. FSE Companion '26: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on the Foundations of Software Engineering. doi:10.1145/3803437.3804438

citation: Zhiqiang Yuan; Mingwei Liu; Shiji Ding; Kaixin Wang; Yixuan Chen; Xin Peng; Yiling Lou (2024). Evaluating and Improving ChatGPT for Unit Test Generation. https://doi.org/10.1145/3660783

citation: AI-Powered Unit Test Generation via Multi-LLM Chaining: A Case Study With GPT-4o, Gemini, and Claude-3.5. DOI: 10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3637221
tool_llm: Gemini; GPT-4o; Claude-3.5 Sonnet; Gemini+GPT-4o; Gemini+Claude-3.5.

citation: The Impact of Prompt Programming on Function-Level Code Generation. DOI: 10.1109/TSE.2025.3587794
tool_llm: GPT-4o; Llama3-70B-Instruct; Mistral-Small-Instruct-2409; older GPT-3.5/Llama2 data also collected.
dataset: CodePromptEval: 221 CoderEval Python tasks × 32 prompt combinations = 7,072 prompts; each run three times.
setting: Full factorial: few-shot, CoT, persona, function signature, package list.
metric: Pass@k/test correctness; CrystalBLEU similarity; code smells; cyclomatic/cognitive complexity; failure types.
main_result: Function signature or few-shot context can improve correctness; combining many prompt techniques generally does not reliably improve results. Failure increases with harder dependency levels. Syntactic failure is explicitly separated: GPT-4o ~0.4%, Llama3 ~0.9%, Mistral ~1.5% of 7,072 tasks averaged over runs. Semantic and operational failures are reported separately; overall pass: GPT-4o 52.2%, Llama3 50.5%, Mistral 46.9%.
code_available: See source paper / replication package where stated
limitations: Function generation rather than test generation; Python rather than Java/JUnit; results depend on CoderEval and selected prompt formulations.
rq_relevance: High methodology support: freeze prompt; classify task/dependency difficulty; do not confound models with prompt variation.

citation: On the Effectiveness of LLM-as-a-Judge for Code Generation and Summarization. DOI: 10.1109/TSE.2025.3586082
dataset: CoderEval code generation: 230 Java + 230 Python problems initially; after benchmark QA, 184 Java + 190 Python retained. Code summarization: 1,163 summaries.
setting: Several judging prompts including zero-shot, rationale, automated CoT and slow-thinking variants.
metric: Agreement/confusion matrix vs test execution; Cohen's kappa; human agreement for summarization.
main_result: GPT-4-turbo is the strongest judge but still often misjudges code correctness; execution-based tests remain the more reliable oracle in this setup. Not a unit-test generation paper; it performs quality assurance on benchmark test suites and generated implementations before judging. Test execution is used as the correctness oracle; even GPT-4-turbo frequently misjudges incorrect implementations as correct.
code_available: See source paper / replication package where stated
limitations: Two tasks only; Java/Python only; findings depend on prompt variants and benchmark quality.
rq_relevance: High methodology support: our experiment should use compiler/JUnit execution as ground truth rather than model self-evaluation.
